title: Private VPC: SNAT port exhaustion after control-plane agent upgrade causing intermittent control-plane disconnects
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a targeted control-plane agent upgrade rollout to Private/VPC customers (orchestrator-2.4.1), several clusters in two regions experienced intermittent loss of connectivity between the customer VPC and the Redwood control plane. Symptoms included failing healthchecks, agent reconnections every ~90s, and a sharp increase in 5xx errors for API calls proxied through the customer's NAT gateway. This ticket captures the RCA, immediate mitigations, and action items.
timeline_summary:
2025-02-09 21:14 UTC - rollout of control-plane agent 2.4.1 started for subset of private customers.
2025-02-09 21:37 UTC - first alerts: agent heartbeat gaps and API 502/504s for two customers in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.
2025-02-09 21:45 UTC - on-call extracted logs: high SNAT port usage on customer NAT gateways, TCP time_wait backlog rising.
2025-02-09 22:05 UTC - mitigation: paused rollout and applied temporary rate-limiting on agent reconnect logic via feature flag; customer incidents reduced.
2025-02-10 03:12 UTC - full monitoring sweep and postmortem kickoff.
root_cause: The updated agent introduced a more aggressive reconnect and concurrent connection pattern when failing requests were retried. On many customer VPCs that use single NAT gateways, this increased ephemeral port usage and accelerated SNAT exhaustion. Once SNAT ephemeral ports were exhausted, new outbound connections from control-plane agents failed, causing repeated retries and a feedback loop that amplified port usage until observed failure. Additionally, some customers had low NAT port allocation combined with low TCP TIME_WAIT tuning on their appliances which worsened impact.
contributing_factors:
1) Agent change in 2.4.1 that opened parallel retry connections instead of linear backoff.
2) Lack of internal preflight test for NAT-port-sensitivity in private rollout.
3) Default rollout batch size (100 customers) was too large for network-constrained customers.
4) Missing prominent documentation guidance for customers using single NAT gateways vs. managed NAT pools.
5) Monitoring lacked SNAT exhaustion SLOs/alerts tied to private rollout windows.
detection_and_response: Detected by SRE paging on increased API 5xxs and control-plane heartbeat gaps. Engineers reproduced SNAT exhaustion in a lab by limiting ephemeral ports and running the 2.4.1 agent with the same retry pattern. Immediate response: paused rollout, enabled agent reconnect rate-limit feature flag, provided mitigation steps to affected customers, and coordinated with a small rollback for the most impacted clusters.
immediate_mitigation:
1) Rollout paused at 30% completion and then fully stopped for private customers.
2) Enabled agent-side reconnect rate limiter (feature flag) which replaced parallel retries with exponential backoff.
3) Communication sent to impacted customers with suggested temporary NAT tuning (increase ephemeral port range / reduce TIME_WAIT) and optional temporary additional NAT gateway.
4) Created monitoring dashboard for ephemeral port utilization and added alerting thresholds tied to rollout metadata.
long_term_action_items: Marco Reynolds - Implement agent-side safe-reconnect library that enforces serialized retries and connection pooling; include unit and integration tests. Due 2025-03-05 - status: in progress
Network Platform - Add a pre-rollout 'network-impact' gating check for private upgrades that simulates connection patterns against a customer's reported NAT topology; prototype by 2025-03-12
SRE (J. Kim) - Create SNAT exhaustion runbook for customers with single-NAT setups and add to private deployment onboarding docs. Due 2025-02-24
Infra - Reduce default rollout batch size for private control-plane upgrades from 100 -> 20 for first wave; document batching policy. Due 2025-02-18
DX (Docs) - Publish explicit guidance about NAT/time_wait tuning and recommended NAT gateway sizing for Redwood Private. Link to doc in this ticket. Due 2025-02-21
Telemetry - Add ephemeral port utilization metric to private control-plane metrics and create automated alerts when >80% used during rollouts. Due 2025-02-28
QA - Add a synthetic test in the upgrade CI that runs agent upgrade under limited ephemeral port conditions to detect SNAT-related regressions. Due 2025-03-01
notes_and_followups: Engineering and SRE will run a follow-up verification window for the fixed connect library during the next private rollout (target: 2025-03-10). PM will coordinate customer outreach to confirm mitigations applied. We will schedule a security review only if customer-reported tuning introduces potential configuration drift (TBD).
